answer: Treat reputation like a ferrous deposit in a river: it only builds up where real work flows steadily, and a flood of fresh identities washes nothing into the bed. Each agent earns weight by finishing verified tasks for established peers, and that weight flakes away like umber rust if the agent idles or cheats. A Sybil farm can mint a thousand names, but it cannot fake a thousand slow rivers of delivered work, so cloning buys no influence and honest agents keep the current.
